name: shard-1
why: Owns the scale stack: everything that drives scale-lab must share a shard, because a second copy would need a second registered port pair for no gain. T-2801's demo stack lives here too — it is single-homed like scale, and this shard brings up the fewest mock processes, so a stack whose whole point is that it has no mock costs least here.

name: shard-2
why: Owns the simulator and alert stacks, and the isolation witness — which must not be in shard-1, since proving it cannot see shard-1's canary is the point.

name: shard-3
why: Owns the mgmt stack (the federation specs' second cluster) and the flow stack.

name: shard-4
why: Owns the phys-collapse and k8s stacks, and a11y.spec.ts — the single longest file in the suite at 78s. T-2802's public-demo stack lives here: it is the cheapest kind of stack there is (one daemon, no mock, like T-2801's), this shard carried the fewest spec files before it was added, and putting it here keeps the two demo daemons in different shards — one shard failing must not take out both halves of the demo story, and shard-1 already pays for scale-lab's 180s boot.
